# OCS2 URDF BuildModel (pinocchio::urdf::buildModel) Enters Eigen aligned_free and Segmentation Fault, While Same Function Works in Other Examples, How to Locate and Handle the Original Thread?

> **Current answer:** Maintainers first trace back from aligned_free, finding that different Eigen vectorization/CPU compilation options were used in the same process. They recommend all dependencies use find_package(pinocchio REQUIRED) and pinocchio::pinocchio. The author found that removing -march=native in one library resolved the issue. Therefore, the main issue is cross-library ABI and compilation option consistency; it cannot be simply attributed to buildModel or URDF itself.

## Key terms

- Application Binary Interface (ABI) (应用二进制接口)
- Vectorization Flags (向量化编译选项)
- Imported Target (导入目标)
- Aligned Allocator (对齐分配器)
- Segmentation Fault (段错误)

## Problem and symptoms

- What should be checked first when a Pinocchio URDF buildModel call fails after adding another Pinocchio dependency library?
- crash during pinocchio::urdf::buildModel in Eigen aligned allocator free path; GDB backtrace into JointModelCompositeTpl destructor.
- The function works in other examples, but fails only when both libraries that depend on Pinocchio are linked.

## Environment

- Ubuntu Focal; Pinocchio 2.6.20 amd64; OCS2 getPinocchioInterfaceFromUrdfModel; two indirect dependencies use CMake package and pkg-config.

## Priority diagnostics

- Compare all linked libraries' compilers, Eigen vectorization options, and -march options, not just URDF content.
- Compare how each library accesses Pinocchio; the maintainer recommends using pinocchio::pinocchio imported target to propagate dependencies and compilation defines.

## Possible causes

- The maintainer points out that different vectorization compilation options lead to different malloc/free paths in Eigen; the author later finds that library A alone enabled -march=native.

## Attempts

- Maintainers provided two CMake write styles, both using find_package(pinocchio REQUIRED) and target_link_libraries(... pinocchio::pinocchio).
- The author removed -march=native from just one library.

## Effective fixes

- Ensure all Pinocchio/Eigen dependencies in the same process use compatible and consistent compilation options; removing -march=native in one library resolved the issue.
- CMake projects should prioritize linking pinocchio::pinocchio, and no longer manually concatenate Pinocchio/Eigen include, library, and compilation defines from different libraries.

## Result

- The author explicitly reports the segmentation fault disappeared after removing -march=native in library A; the maintainer adds that such mixed use is not unique to Pinocchio and closes the issue as completed.

## Limitations

- The original post does not provide a unified compilation after the build; cannot attribute all buildModel errors to -march=native.
- The root cause is in-consistent compilation options within the same process, not -march=native in all projects.

## Safety notes

- Before deploying WBC on real hardware, run URDF loading and dynamics smoke tests on a build product matching the target CPU to avoid ABI issues during control process startup.
